Subject: PO + invoice cadence for proposed Dedicated commit

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — leadership is supportive and we're ready to move toward a 12-month Dedicated commitment. Finance has asked me to send the draft PO and confirm two procurement items before we route internally:

1) MedCorp requires PO acceptance on our side referencing vendor tax ID. Can Redwood accept PO metadata on the invoice (PO number + vendor tax ID) and include a purchase-order line on each invoice?
2) We need an invoice cadence that supports tranche payments: monthly billing for subscription usage, but an advance tranche to be captured at contract signature (equal to first two months), then monthly thereafter. Are you able to issue an initial advance-invoice and then monthly statements tied to the PO number?

I'm attaching the draft PO (MedCorp_PO_202611.pdf) and a redlined SOW for your records. If this is workable we can route to our legal and the finance director, Kevin, for final sign-off.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if it's easier.

Best,
Elise Martin
Senior Procurement Manager
MedCorp Health

Hi Elise — great to hear you're moving forward. Short answers first: yes on PO metadata and per-invoice PO line; yes on an advance invoice for the initial tranche. A few clarifying details so we can align internal billing: 

- Vendor tax ID: please confirm the exact string you want printed on the invoices (MedCorp provided TIN or specific subsidiary). We can map that to the invoice header and the per-line PO field.
- Advance tranche: we typically issue a pro-forma invoice at signature for the upfront amount; Redwood's billing team will need the PO number to be referenced on that invoice so your AP can match. The advance would be refundable against subsequent invoices as credits.
- Invoice cadence: we can do monthly invoices with a running PO number and apply the advance credit across the first two monthly invoices, or we can show a separate "Advance Payment" line that is applied as a negative line on month 2. Which presentation does your ERP prefer?
- Discount ladder: my commercial note — for a 12-month committed Dedicated block at the capacity you demoed we can offer a tiered discount: 5% at signature, 10% once ARR thresholds are met (two-quarter review), or a straight 8% if you prefer a single guaranteed discount. I want to make sure pricing presentation doesn't conflict with your procurement tagging.

Copying Grace (billing) and Aditya (finance) to confirm implementation details on our side; Grace — can Redwood issue the initial advance pro-forma invoice and include the PO metadata exactly as supplied? Aditya — do you see any revenue recognition impacts with the advance setup that would affect contract language?

If helpful, I can propose formal invoice line examples in a follow-up.

–Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com

Kimberly / Aditya — quick internal note on billing mechanics so we respond consistently to MedCorp: 

1) We can print the vendor tax ID and PO number on each invoice (header + per-line). We need the exact TIN string and legal entity name to match our accounting tags.
2) Advance tranche / pro-forma: we will create an invoice with type "Advance payment" that is posted to AR and then applied as a credit to subsequent invoices. We will clearly reference the PO on the advance so AP teams can apply it.
3) Presentation options for ERP matching: some ERPs prefer a single line per invoice with a PO reference; others want both the PO number and a line-level PO reference. We can support both but would like MedCorp to confirm which matching rule they use (header-only vs line-level).

Also FYI for revenue recognition: Aditya — if we capture an advance equal to two months of committed capacity we will treat it as deferred revenue and then recognize monthly as services are delivered. Please confirm if the finance team needs any special contract clause language for the deferred revenue treatment.

I'll draft two sample invoice PDFs (header-only PO vs line-level PO) and attach them in the next reply.

Grace O'Connor
Billing Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

Team — thanks for the quick breakdown. One commercial ask from my side before we finalize: MedCorp asked for a slab discount tied to committed capacity tiers. Our preferred approach:

- Add a Tiered Discount Appendix in the SOW that enumerates thresholds (e.g., 100k monthly GPU hours => 10% discount; 250k => 15%).
- For the initial signature offer we give a guaranteed 6% applied at invoice level; once the customer hits usage thresholds the higher slab applies retroactively to the start of the quarter and we issue a credit.

This keeps the PO/invoice structure simple (discount applied as a single invoice-level credit) while meeting procurement's need for predictable discounting. Kimberly — please position this to Elise as an operational-friendly approach that reduces PO complexity. Grace — if acceptable we'll need the billing system to support retroactive crediting and a quarterly reconciliation report. Aditya — flag anything material for revenue ops.

Vivek
Sr. Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
